title: IPO
statement_short: Suppose LeetCode is going to start its IPO. Given w initial capital, k maximum projects to complete, and arrays for profits and capital requirements of each project, pick at most k distinct projects to maximize final capital.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 10^5, 0 <= w <= 10^9, n == profits.length == capital.length, 1 <= n <= 10^5, 0 <= profits[i], capital[i] <= 10^4
hint: Limit k and n up to 10^5 dictates greedily picking max profit projects from a max-heap of currently affordable projects.
why_not: Right: Heap / Priority Queue paired with sorting by capital dynamically yields the maximum available profit project in O(n log n + k log n) time. Not Greedy: Pure greedy search without a priority queue scans all affordable projects repeatedly in O(k \* n) time. Not 1D DP: Dynamic programming state caching does not apply due to large capital bounds up to 10^9\. Not Sorting: Sorting alone orders projects statically by capital, but dynamic capital increases require heap-based max profit extraction.
complexity: O(n log n + k log n) time, O(n) space
